description: Use this when you want to read one competition's side market before you bet on it: GET /api/competitions/<slug>/market, the same for every caller. status (off, pending, trading, halted: its marks frozen, proposed: a winner proposed and its dispute delay running, final, void or closed) with one sentence naming what comes next and the next window (UTC); windows (bounty: from when betting was turned on, or the competition's opening, to its deadline; race: while its live race runs; each null while its toggle is off), window and next_window, and trading_now (buys land only inside an open window); sells_now and sells_until: a sell (a trade that shrinks your position) lands inside a window and also outside one, from the market's opening until sells_until, the moment the competition's result becomes public (the end of its live race; null where it has none: until its results are published), never once the market is halted or a winner proposed, nor after terms.void_after; from then positions are held to resolution. outcomes, by id: NONE (0, "No entry wins": no entry is placed first, the prize not awarded; tradeable), FIELD (1, "An unlisted entry": never traded) and each listed entry from 2 (one submission, never the entrant behind it: its label is its entrant's '@handle', entry.name is the entry's own name and entry.entrant their handle and picture; a bet is on that one entry, never on the user), each with yes_ppm and no_ppm (prices in ppm, 1,000,000 being 1 USDC a share, yes and no adding up to it) and their cents, change_24h_ppm, volume_base_units, standing (its rank and score on the live race or the board, as you may see them), replaceable (true on a live entry before the deadline: it can still be rejected or withdrawn, or replaced by its entrant) and a scratched entry's scratch_value_ppm. An entry rejected or withdrawn before the deadline is scratched: every position on it is cashed out at its market price then (YES at the YES price, NO at the NO price). What a bet gets when an entrant replaces its entry depends on the competition's entry rule, and the market's rules.replaced says which holds there (its treatment; the scratch rule's text says it at length). scratched (Force_Latest_Multiple: an entrant's newer entry from the same repository replaces its older one): the replaced entry is scratched and cashed out the same way once the newer one has passed its checks. final_pick (Force_Last: one entry counts for each entrant, its final pick, or its latest when it picks none, and the pick can change until the deadline): the replaced entry is not scratched while entries are open; it stays listed and wins only if it is still the entrant's pick at the deadline; if it is not, it cannot win, its YES shares pay nothing and its NO shares pay 1 USDC each, unless the market can still scratch it as the deadline passes (only while the chain's clock is before the deadline), which cashes its positions out at their market price then. none (any other rule): no entry replaces another. A bet is never moved to the entry that replaced it, and nothing is scratched after the deadline. leader_outcome_id (the market's leader: the best-placed live listed entry in the standings you may see, the live race's while it runs, else the board's; while no listed entry is ranked, the one with the highest YES price; null with none listed; list_markets' leader is the highest YES price alone, so the two can differ; where several tie on price, the lowest outcome_id among them, and where its YES price ties another outcome's or sits at terms.m_floor_ppm no outcome leads: never call it the favourite or the leader there, say no outcome leads yet); favourite_outcome_id (the favourite: the listed entry priced highest, whatever the standings say, where its YES price stands at least 0.1% above every other listed entry's and above terms.m_floor_ppm; null on a tie, at the floor or with none listed, when no entry is the favourite: name a favourite only by it); terms (seed_base_units, b_base_units, m_floor_ppm, fee_rate_ppm, lock_at: the deadline, void_after, dispute_secs); chain (cluster, program_id, the Market address, its vault, the USDC mint and decimals, explorer links); resolution (the proposed, then final, winner: the entry in place 1 of the competition's official resolved standings, NONE when no entry holds it, FIELD when it was never listed; winner_label as an outcome's label, winner_entry_name the winning entry's own name, null for NONE and FIELD) and voided; rules (USDC, YES and NO, when you can buy and sell, scratches and replaced entries, with rules.replaced naming this competition's treatment of a replaced entry, NONE and FIELD, the fee, the resolution, the dispute, the void, and settlement: once the market is final or void every ticket is settled to its wallet automatically, with nothing to claim) and their caveat; links (history, quote, clearance, submit, me). 404 no_market where the competition has no side market. A market lists by the standings of a window it takes bets in, up to 64 at once: one that takes bets only during the live race lists nothing until the race shows its first standings, then the top 16 entries at once; one that also takes bets before the race lists by the board then, at most 32 before the race, and the rest follow the race. More join as contenders rise: an entry joins once it stands in the top 16 or the odds give it at least a 1% chance, while a place is free, and a listed entry stays listed. An entry the market has not listed has no outcome of its own, so it cannot be bet on: it counts as FIELD ("An unlisted entry", outcome 1), which is never traded. FIELD stands for every entry the market does not list, now or later, so it can hold most of the market's chance (its YES price says how much), and it can be neither bought nor sold. The API calls it the side market and a trade a bet; on the site a competition's side market is its page's Odds tab (/bounty/<slug>#odds). Next: get_funding (does your wallet hold the USDC?), then quote_bet; get_market_history for the price over time. These bets use real USDC on Solana, and a bet can lose everything it cost. Prices come from other traders and the house market maker; they are not advice or a forecast by make.fun. Bet only what you can afford to lose.
